past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If the particles of a medium vibrate in the direction of propagation of the wave, then it is called a/ an
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: In a longitudinal wave, the particles of the medium vibrate back and forth along the same direction (parallel) in which the wave is propagating.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If the frequency of a wave is doubled, then the time period of the wave will
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: The time period ($T$) and frequency ($f$) are inversely proportional to each other, given by the relation $T = \frac{1}{f}$. If the frequency is doubled ($2f$), the time period becomes $\frac{1}{2f}$, which is half of the original time period.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text: If the time period of a simple pendulum is 2 s on the surface of the Earth, then the time period of the same pendulum on the surface of the Moon will be
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{L}{g}}$. Since the acceleration due to gravity on the Moon ($g_m$) is less than that on Earth ($g_e$) ($g_m \approx \frac{1}{6}g_e$), a smaller value of $g$ results in a larger time period $T$. Therefore, the time period on the Moon will be greater than 2 s.

past_paper_mcqs.stem_text:
If a mechanical wave moves from a rare to the denser medium, then which of the following factors will change during refraction?
I. Wavelength
II. Speed of the wave
III. Frequency of the wave
past_paper_mcqs.explanation: During refraction, the frequency of a wave remains constant because it depends solely on the source. However, both the speed of the wave and its wavelength change when transitioning between media of different densities.

crqs.question: Differentiate between transverse waves and longitudinal waves with two examples of each.
crqs.answer: In transverse waves, particles vibrate perpendicular to wave propagation (e.g., water waves, light waves). In longitudinal waves, particles vibrate parallel to wave propagation creating compressions and rarefactions (e.g., sound waves in air, slinky compression waves).

erqs.question: A simple pendulum is attached to a 4 m long string. Find its time period on Earth (g = 9.8 m/s²) and explain how the time period changes if the elevator accelerates upward or is on the Moon.
erqs.answer: On stationary Earth: T = 2π√(l/g) = 2π√(4 / 9.8) = 4.01 s. On the Moon (g_m = g/6), T increases by √6. In an upward-accelerating elevator (g_eff = g + a), T decreases.
erqs.source: AKU-EB SSC-II Model Paper II Q.6(a)
